title: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels Ltd - 544111 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, but PAT fell 14% to close to Rs.12 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone operating revenue was Rs.167 crore (up 8% YoY) and EBITDA Rs.47 crore (up 3%, margin 28.12%), with occupancy held at 92%. PAT declined about 14% YoY on higher finance costs tied to the Zillion (Juhu) acquisition and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax charge from moving to the new tax regime. Management guided to stronger ADR and RevPAR from Q2 onward, citing BRICS Summit, conferences and the wedding season. Expansion plans were reiterated: 42 hotels/2,677 keys to 3,149 keys by FY27-end, and more than 6,000 keys by FY30, with Flurys targeted at 140 outlets by FY27-end and 400 by 2030.

financial_highlights.value: close to Rs.12 crore (PAT margin close to 7%)
Rs.4.79 crore, of which about Rs.2.7 crore from mutual funds

segments.name: Hotels (Park / Zone brands)
segments.commentary: Occupancy held at 92%, described as India's leading occupancy; portfolio is 42 hotels with 2,677 keys. Ran Baas (Patiala) ARR is about Rs.33,000 and Lotus Palace (Chettinad) about Rs.13,000, both still stabilising.

segments.name: Flurys (F&B cafes)
segments.commentary: 111 outlets across cafes, kiosks and tea rooms after a new Visakhapatnam outlet; first standalone Gurugram cafe opened in August. Plan is 29 more outlets to reach 140 by FY27-end and 400 by 2030, on an asset-light model; 21.5% outlet CAGR since 2019 (17 outlets).

segments.name: EM Bypass Kolkata (hotel plus service apartments)
segments.commentary: 33 of 69 service apartments sold at average realisation about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; Rs.21 crore received so far, with Rs.70-80 crore cash inflow expected in FY27. Project completion targeted early 2030.

guidance_outlook: ADR growth expected to be high single digit from Q2 onward, helped by the BRICS Summit in Delhi, about 40 wedding dates from November to March, and trade shows (Aero Show Bangalore, Bharat Mobility Expo).
Hotel pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27, taking the portfolio to 3,149 keys by year-end; plan to double hotels to 87 hotels and 6,719 keys over four years.
Flurys targeted at 140 outlets by FY27-end and 400 by 2030; management also cited a goal of 100 Flurys outlets in West Bengal by its centenary next year.
Other income expected at about Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter, with further increase expected as about Rs.50 crore more EM Bypass cash comes in by year-end.
Tax rate expected to fall from about 35% to 25-30% range as the company moves to the new regime from Q2.

Capex of about Rs.1,140 crore for five projects over 4-5 years, plus acquisition and renovation spend of about Rs.350 crore (Zillion Juhu, Kochi Malabar House). Within FY27, Rs.200-250 crore of capex is expected.
capex_capacity: New properties: Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250 rooms), Visakhapatnam (100 rooms), EM Bypass Kolkata (220 rooms) and Jaipur (150 rooms), with capex of about Rs.1.2 crore per room, so about Rs.1,140 crore over 4-5 years.
The Park Mumbai at Juhu (78 rooms, converted from 60 service apartments): design phase complete, launch targeted October 2027; long-term financing tied up for the Zillion property.

Vizag 100-room hotel: project teams on site, launch expected in the current month, completion early 2030. Kochi Malabar House (17 keys, about half an acre) acquisition expected to close October-November 2026 for about Rs.64 crore.
Pune FSI increased from 2.5 lakh sq ft to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan to use 2.5 lakh sq ft for hotel and 4+ lakh sq ft for residential.

Ongoing operational capex of Rs.40 crore per year for 4-5 years, plus Flurys capex of Rs.40 crore per year. Net capex after EM Bypass contribution about Rs.1,500 crore, to be funded from about Rs.240-250 crore EBITDA and debt headroom.
SAP S/4HANA for Finance implemented during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Q1 headwinds: West Asia crisis, oil-price pressure, near-flat domestic air traffic and about 10% decline in international air traffic into India. All-India ADR growth was 6%; Mumbai air passengers fell 3.5%, Hyderabad over 12% and Chennai 13%.
Management expects ADR growth in the high single digits from Q2 as conditions stabilise, and says Q2-Q4 should be distinctly better than Q1.
Juhu (Mumbai) ARRs cited at Rs.18,000-20,000, with Mumbai ARR growth of 10-15%; Juhu acquisition cost about Rs.40,000 per sq ft versus market levels of about Rs.1 lakh per sq ft.
Kolkata has the lowest metro inventory at 5,111 keys and Visakhapatnam is also supply-short, which management cites as supporting high ARR at new openings.
Flurys acquisition pipeline: Adani Group (airports), Phoenix Mills and DLF nationwide deals close to signing, and PVR deal for about 10 outlets close to finalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Given 92% occupancy, how will ADR evolve and what long-term growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects high single-digit ARR growth from the coming season, supported by BRICS Summit, weddings and trade shows, and by stabilisation at Ran Baas and Lotus Palace.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Flurys outlet additions behind earlier plans, and how will the 29 additions be phased?
qa_highlights.answer: Five outlets have opened; 29 more are planned in FY27: 5 in Pune, 3 in Mumbai, 5 in Hyderabad, about 7 in NCR and 4 in Bengaluru, with PVR and Phoenix/DLF deals in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.2.7 crore mutual fund income sustainable, and how will other income change?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khosla said about Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter is sustainable; Vijay Dewan said other income should rise further with EM Bypass cash inflows and about Rs.97 crore of mutual funds.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 14% PAT decline, and what will the tax rate be going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs rose about Rs.2.5 crore YoY from Zillion acquisition financing, and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax charge was taken; tax rate is 40% this quarter, expected to fall to about 25-30% from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex split and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Net capex of about Rs.1,500 crore after EM Bypass, to be funded from about Rs.1,300 crore of internal accruals over 4-5 years; Rs.200-250 crore of capex is expected within FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How do the service apartment model and mixed-use development affect return on capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects EM Bypass sales of Rs.300-325 crore to fund the hotel build, and expects ROCE to rise from about 9-10% toward 20%+ and double by 2030.

risks_watch: ADR recovery depends on the air-travel and geopolitical backdrop; Q1 showed pressure from West Asia, oil prices and weak air traffic.
PAT pressure from rising finance costs (Zillion acquisition financing) and the transition to the new tax regime, including the Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax charge.
Flurys outlet additions must reach 29 in roughly seven months to hit the 140-outlet FY27 target; several partner deals are still pending.
EM Bypass service apartment sales (33 of 69 sold) drive the Rs.70-80 crore FY27 cash inflow and the self-funding model; pace and price realisation need monitoring.
New hotels (Juhu, Vizag, Kolkata, Pune) are scheduled to open between October 2027 and 2030; delays would affect the 3,149-key FY27 target and longer-term keys goal.
Investor-relations responsiveness on the mutual fund portfolio disclosure was questioned on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand recovery, Flurys expansion and EM Bypass cash flows, but defensive on the PAT decline, which was attributed to finance costs and a one-time-like tax transition. Some answers lacked precision on the guidance numbers (for example ADR growth and tax rates), and a question on mutual fund holdings was handled offline.
key_quotes: So, we expect that the quarters ahead are going to be distinctly better than the quarter which has gone by.
So, we can expect definitely high single digit ARR growth as we go forward.
So, expect good ARR growth as we move forward.

adds.what: 12 hotels / 472 keys pipeline taking portfolio to 3,149 keys by FY27-end
The Park Mumbai at Juhu, 78 rooms converted from service apartments
Five new properties (Pune 200, Navi Mumbai 250, Vizag 100, EM Bypass Kolkata 220, Jaipur 150 rooms) for about Rs.1,140 crore capex over 4-5 years

growth.why: Guides to high single-digit ADR growth from Q2 and 3,149 keys by FY27-end (12 hotels, 472-key pipeline), backed by a named pipeline and a Rs.1,140 crore capex plan, though demand conditions are soft and the Q1 EBITDA growth was modest.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin was 28.12% with EBITDA up only 3% vs revenue up 8%, and management expects ADR high single digit from Q2 with Q2-Q4 'distinctly better' than Q1, but the new tax regime and Zillion finance costs cut PAT by 14% and no explicit margin target was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Vizag launch Q2 FY27; 12 hotels/472 keys by Q4 FY27
rows.why: 12 hotels with 472 keys (17.6% of the 2,677-key base) are under construction for FY27-end, Vizag 100 rooms is on site with launch expected this month, but Juhu (Oct 2027) and the five new properties (Rs.1,140 crore over 4-5 years) fall beyond the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupancy is already 92%, and management guides high single-digit ADR growth from Q2 with 472 new keys added by FY27-end, so room-night growth should follow from the pipeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Rs.200-250 crore of capex is expected within FY27 and Rs.1,140 crore across five approved projects over 4-5 years, with Kochi Malabar House acquisition (about Rs.64 crore) closing Oct-Nov 2026 and utilisation at 92%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided high single-digit ADR growth and 3,149 keys by FY27-end, but Q1 EBITDA grew only 3% standalone and demand headwinds (West Asia, oil, international air traffic down about 10%) are unresolved, so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Flurys needs 29 outlets in about seven months to reach 140 with several partner deals (PVR, Phoenix, DLF, Adani) still pending, and new hotel delays would hit the 3,149-key target; the call's Q1 ADR growth was only 6% all-India.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Flurys plans 29 more outlets in FY27 (5 Pune, 3 Mumbai, 5 Hyderabad, about 7 NCR, 4 Bengaluru) and the Vizag 100-room hotel launches this month, Ran Baas and Lotus Palace are still stabilising.

rows.label: EM Bypass service apartment cash inflow
rows.why: 33 of 69 units sold with Rs.21 crore received so far, and Rs.70-80 crore inflow expected in FY27 plus about Rs.50 crore more by year-end, against net debt-to-EBITDA of 0.70.

rows.label: High single-digit ADR growth from Q2
rows.why: Management cites BRICS Summit, about 40 wedding dates Nov-Mar and trade shows, with Q1 all-India ADR growth at 6% and Mumbai ARR growth of 10-15%.

rows.label: Tax rate step-down to 25-30%
rows.why: Tax rate is 40% this quarter and expected to fall from about 35% to 25-30% as the company moves to the new regime, after a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax charge.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand recovery, Flurys expansion and EM Bypass cash flows, but defensive on the 14% PAT decline and vague on the ADR and tax numbers; analysts pressed on the PAT drop and mutual fund disclosure, which was handled offline.
